title: Encrypted DNS Discovery RFC 9463 Generic DNR Information Architecture
purpose: Define the generic DNR information behavior shared by RFC 9463 DHCPv4, DHCPv6, and Neighbor Discovery encodings.
design_summary: The generic DNR information slice proves the common RFC 9463 behavior that sits above individual transport encodings: normalized ADN presence, usable resolver-address preservation and filtering, preference-order preservation for multiple addresses, service-priority exposure, RFC 9460 SvcParam wire encoding, ADN-only mode availability, DHCPv6 ORO requestability, OPTION_V6_DNR non-singleton status, and DHCPv4 option data length semantics.
data_and_state_considerations: The slice owns scalar DNR information and byte-level option metadata only. It does not own router interface selection, DHCP lease state, Router Advertisement socket state, or platform resolver installation.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Missing ADN, missing usable addresses, and invalid service parameter keys are rejected.
Loopback and multicast addresses are filtered without reordering remaining resolver addresses.
ADN-only mode is available in DHCPv4, DHCPv6, and Neighbor Discovery helper surfaces.
OPTION_V6_DNR is requestable in ORO and is not represented as a singleton option.
OPTION_V4_DNR uses the encoded option data length as N and rejects mismatches.
risks: This slice does not prove that a router selected a specific physical LAN-facing interface.
This slice does not implement platform DHCP or Router Advertisement integration.
This slice does not install encrypted DNS resolver configuration into the host operating system.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The generic tests intentionally bind already-existing scalar and wire helpers to the RFC 9463 shared DNR requirements so future platform adapters can reuse the same validated behavior.
